significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish the form-(iii) law that multilingual factual inconsistency has "two additive components," with only the paraphrase-controlled residual scaling with script or typological distance, plus a causal decomposition in which baseline errors arise around mid-layer concept computation while residual errors arise at a "distinct late-layer transition locus." This would establish both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, constraining how distance effects, error localization, and interventions should differ between two independently measurable error classes; Elazar et al.'s 2021 work on consistency across paraphrases makes separating that instability from multilingual disagreement a consequential correction rather than merely another representation probe. The negative branches are also informative: a small baseline would support treating most disagreement as language-specific, while shared localization or equal distance dependence would rule out the proposed two-component explanation; true and false therefore identify distinct states of the world. After topic substitution, generic questions about language-independent versus language-specific mechanisms would not merit this score—the specific additive law, differential distance scaling, and two-stage causal account are false of the median hypothesis on this topic and justify the higher rating.

reach.justification: The transferable handle is the explicitly defined "LANGUAGE-SPECIFIC RESIDUAL = cross-lingual disagreement across paraphrase-matched prompts minus the pooled within-language baseline," a diagnostic metric that leaderboard designers and factuality auditors could report instead of total disagreement. It is principally post hoc because it scores inconsistency after answers have been elicited, but it supports non-researcher uptake by people who audit, compare, gate, or release multilingual models rather than serving only mechanistic-interpretability researchers. After per-model remeasurement, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—additive separation and distance scaling in the residual, not merely a procedure for rediscovering an arbitrary direction—and the hypothesis states this across multilingual factual QA and multiple model families, though it does not claim transfer beyond factual answering. The topic-substitution check lowers no further: the topic alone supplies neither this audit metric nor its decomposition, but the absence of ex-ante lead time and the domain restriction keep the reach below the top band.
